title: OU 63, Texas 14: Quentin Griffin's Six-TD Day in the 2000 Rout
question: What happened in the 2000 Oklahoma vs Texas game when OU won 63-14?
answer: On October 7, 2000, No. 10 Oklahoma beat No. 11 Texas 63-14 in Dallas. Quentin Griffin ran for a school-record six touchdowns, OU led 42-0 in the second quarter, and Texas finished with minus-7 rushing yards.
summary: OU crushed Texas 63-14 in 2000 as Quentin Griffin ran for a school-record six touchdowns and the Longhorns finished with minus-7 rushing yards.
body: If you want a single afternoon that announced Oklahoma was back in the national picture, October 7, 2000, is a strong pick. The 10th-ranked Sooners met No. 11 Texas at the Cotton Bowl and won 63-14, a result that still makes Sooner fans grin.

The game was over almost before it started. Oklahoma scored touchdowns on its first five possessions and led 42-0 with 4:43 left in the second quarter. Linebacker Rocky Calmus chipped in a 41-yard interception return for a touchdown along the way, and the Sooners were up by 42 before Texas finally scored.

Running back Quentin Griffin was the star. He scored six rushing touchdowns, a school record, on runs of 1, 4, 8, 1, 8 and 1 yards. Quarterback Josh Heupel was efficient, completing 17 of 27 passes for 275 yards and a touchdown, and the Sooners piled up 534 total yards, their most ever against Texas at the time.

The defense may have been even more impressive. Oklahoma held the Longhorns to minus-7 rushing yards, a Texas school-record low. It was the most lopsided loss Texas had suffered since a 66-3 home defeat to UCLA in 1997.
The rout moved OU to 5-0 and became one of the signature wins of a season that ended with a national championship. It also kicked off a stretch of Sooner dominance in the series in the early 2000s.
